                                                 plot(seq(0, input$flips), seq(0, 1, 1/input$flips), type = "n",

                                                 abline(h = input$p.head, lty = 2, col = "gray")

Unless you want to make a GIF, at least as far as I know, shiny is the most interactive tool available.

You could do something like this with actionButton. Then every time a student clicks the button another step is taken (e.g., another coin is flipped). This requires shiny-incubator.

An easier approach might be to use numericInput where students can increase the number and the output changes immediately.

Yuhei Xie had a project on Github called appstat that had interactive Shiny apps that can be used in teaching. Not sure what happend to that.
